title: CODATA RDMT – Call for suggested additional terms now open; deadline 10 December 2026
content:
The CODATA Research Data Management Terminology (RDMT) https://vocabs.ardc.edu.au/viewById/685 gathers the key terms needed for a common understanding of the research data management domain. The RDMT is revised by the CODATA RDM Terminology Working Group, shared for public review, and then confirmed and finalised biennially.

The RDMT will be once again revised in 2027. In preparation for this process, we are inviting your ideas for any terms that you feel are missing from the current version (v002) of the Terminology.

Before suggesting terms, please read the RDMT scope statement, available here:

https://codata.org/initiatives/data-science-and-stewardship/rdm-terminology-wg/

Once you have verified that the term you’re interested in is a) in scope; and b) not already present within the Terminology, please add it to our suggested additions form here:

https://forms.gle/YyHGETo3FPwixPGB7

The form will close on 10 December 2026. Terms will be discussed by the 2027 RDMT Working Group.

If you are a RDM expert and interested in committing to the 2027 RDMT Working Group, please look out for the call for applications which will be advertised soon.

title: Affiliated Bodies at the ISC Midterm Membership Meeting
content:
Richard Hartshorn is CODATA Vice-President, and Professor of Chemistry in the School of Physical and Chemical Sciences of the University of Canterbury, Christchurch, New Zealand. He was Secretary General of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) from 2016 to 2023.

Representatives from the ISC Affiliated Bodies met at the ISC Midterm Membership Meeting in Beijing on Thursday 22 October. The Affiliated Bodies are a group of organisations based around specific themes, data and information, and global monitoring and observation.

The meeting began with reports from the organisations present and then developed into a discussion of issues to be raised in the report back to the ISC plenary session:

  • There is increased pressure on funding and that is especially true for projects and organisations that involve international coordination and integration. Many of the Affiliated Bodies are finding it challenging to secure necessary financial support.

title: CDIF-4-XAS Project Final Results and Recommendations
content:
The CDIF-4-XAS project has released its final report outlining results and recommendations: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24057167

The CDIF-4-XAS project addresses the critical challenge of data interoperability within X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS). While XAS is fundamental to diverse scientific fields ranging from physics to environmental science, the lack of standardized metadata and formats hinders the FAIR sharing of data across domains. Existing community standards like XDI and NeXus facilitate internal exchange but often lack the contextualization required for broader reuse. This document outlines the implementation of the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) within the XAS domain to establish a lingua franca for FAIR data exchange.

title: CDIF4EOSC Response to the EOSC Semantic Interoperability Task Force Report ‘Practical Semantic Interoperability Recommendations for the EOSC Federation’
content:
Gregory, A., & Hodson, S. (2026). CDIF4EOSC Response to the EOSC Semantic Interoperability Task Force Report ‘Practical Semantic Interoperability Recommendations for the EOSC Federation’ https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23974722

Writing on behalf of the CDIF4EOSC project, we are very pleased to see the recent publication of “Practical Semantic Interoperability Recommendations for the EOSC Federation” from the EOSC-A Semantic Interoperability Task Force (SITF). This work complements the recent and ongoing developments around the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF), notably as it will be employed within EOSC to facilitate the use of FAIR data and related resources.

This short response highlights the points where CDIF is recommended by SITF and the considerable alignment between the SITF recommendations and CDIF.

title: Science in a Complex World: Why Our Future Depends on More Than Scientific Discovery
content:
Reflections from the Beijing Science Dialogue and International Science Council Midterm Meeting, Beijing, China | 19–23 October 2026

By Ntsundeni Louis Mapatagane (CODATA)

Ntsundeni Louis Mapatagena is Co-chair of CODATA Connect, CODATA’s Early Career Network, Director of Planning and Institutional Intelligence at Walter Sisulu University (WSU), MSc Environmental Sciences, Ph.D Candidate on the readiness of higher education institutions for energy efficiency and emissions reduction.

I travelled to Beijing, China, for the Beijing Science Dialogue and International Science Council (ISC) Midterm Meeting, expecting to engage in conversations about the future of science, international scientific cooperation and the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging technologies. I returned with something more profound: a renewed appreciation that the greatest challenge facing science may not necessarily be our ability to generate knowledge, but our collective ability to translate that knowledge into trust, responsible behaviour, effective policy and meaningful societal change.

title: CDIF Releases Initial Converters for Domain Standards
content:
Resources for the Cross Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) have just been expanded to include a series of converters for metadata encoded in a range of domain standards. These converters are developed in Python, and provide transformations both to and from the relevant CDIF profiles. Each is accompanied by a set of example metadata. The conversions cover Croissant ML, Science on Schema.org (SOSO), DDI Codebook, the FAIR2 specification, DCAT, the NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) Unified Metadata Model – Collections, DDI-CDI, and RO Crate.

The mappings used in the converters are published in the Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM) format, for modification and reuse. The converters use a combination of SSSOM mapping and transforms implemented by the python code; the documentation for each converted explains the workflow.

title: Getting off at the right station: reflections on AI readiness
content:
Cyrus Walther is a doctoral student in the Astroparticle Physics Group at TU Dortmund University; nominated by IUPAP, he has served on the CODATA Executive Committee since 2023. He contributes actively to CODATA’s Early Career Group, CODATA Connect, and to the Task Group on Digital Representation of Units of Measure (DRUM).

From the 19th to the 21st of October, the International Science Council (ISC), in collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Technology (CAST), welcomed the international scientific community to Beijing for the Beijing Science Dialogue. During these three days, topics of transformative impact on science were discussed, among them Artificial Intelligence. As AI especially impacts early- and mid-career researchers, EMCRs from the ISC community suggested including young panellists on the topic. Following a nomination, I had the great honour to receive that invitation from the International Science Council to speak as an early-career scientist on the panel “Responsible AI for global challenges”.

title: A Better Future for Science? Reflections from Beijing
content:
Dr. Pragya Chaube is Assistant Professor at the UPES University, India. She is a co-chair of the CODATA Connect Early Career Network and co-founder Open Science South Asia Network (OSSAN). Pragya’s participation in the International Science Council’s (ISC) Midterm Membership Meeting and Beijing Science Dialogue was kindly supported by the ISC and by the China Association for Science and Technology (CAST).

I had the opportunity to spend the week of 19–24 October in Beijing, alongside a large gathering of scientists and representatives of national science academies from across the globe, reflecting on the future of science. More than 1,000 people from over 80 countries and regions came together for these discussions. We welcomed a new ISC President, Robbert Dijkgraaf, and, on the final day, adopted the Beijing Science Declaration: Science in a Complex World, Science for a Better Future.

The meeting covered many important issues, but I left Beijing reflecting on a question that connects many of them for me: What kind of research ecosystem do we want to build for the future, and what needs to change to get there?

title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: October 2026 Edition
content:
From local resilience to systemic risk governance

Households can prepare for floods, but they cannot decide where development happens upstream, how regional power networks are protected, or whether capital keeps flowing into hazard-prone land. Writing for International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction, Bapon Fakhruddin argues that where disaster impacts are felt should not be confused with who produces the risk. He separates risk creation, risk transmission and risk bearing, noting that those who benefit from a development decision are often not those who bear its consequences. His Local-to-Systemic Risk Governance framework proposes financed local resilience compacts, which pair local responsibility with real decision rights and predictable funding, alongside investment appraisals that make trade-offs explicit. Resilience is experienced locally, he concludes, but it is not produced locally alone.

title: Strong demand for crisis data checklists but few in place, UNESCO and CODATA survey finds
content:
Read the full article on the UNESCO Website.

Strong demand for crisis data checklists but few in place, UNESCO and CODATA survey finds

Most organisations working on disasters, crises and emergencies see value in a checklist for crisis data policies, yet few have one. This is the central finding of a global survey report published by UNESCO and the Committee (ISC) on Data of the International Science Council (CODATA) on 6 October 2026. The findings point to a next phase in which the Data Policies for Times of Crisis (DPTC) Checklist would be tested in practice with interested institutions.
